title: Experiment stage definitions and evaluation SLA schedule
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a canonical set of experiment stages (alpha, internal canary, open canary, ramp, GA) with precise evaluation SLAs and decision gates for Redwood platform experiments. Deliverables: 1) stage definitions and minimum evaluation windows, 2) a prescriptive SLA table for metric evaluation (latency, error rate, cost per token, quality regressions), 3) recommended statistical tests and sample-size guidance, 4) templates for dashboards and alert thresholds, and 5) an operations checklist for staged rollouts. This ticket consolidates PM, Eng, SRE, and Analytics inputs so product teams can run consistent, audit-ready experiments across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A single doc exists that defines the canonical stages and the required minimum evaluation window for each stage
SLA table with metric thresholds and pass/fail rules that PMs and Eng can apply to new experiments
Sample-size calculator guidance and example calculations for 3 common traffic profiles
Dashboards and alert templates specified such that SRE/Analytics can implement within 2 sprints
Sign-offs received from PM, Eng lead, SRE, and Analytics owners

measurement_plan: Primary metrics: 95th latency, request error rate (5xx), cost per 1k tokens, failure rate of structured outputs
Quality regressions: evaluate prompt-level holdout sets; require <1% drop in fidelity for alpha->GA for critical prompts
Statistical tests: two-sided t-test for continuous metrics, Chi-square for categorical failure rates, with alpha=0.01 for canaries and alpha=0.05 for open ramps
Minimum sample sizes: guidance table included in doc with examples for small (10qps), medium (100qps), large (1k+ qps) traffic profiles
Evaluation windows: alpha=24h internal, canary=open=72h rolling, ramp=7 days, GA=30 day monitoring for SLA compliance
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy metrics during short canaries —> Mitigation: require minimum absolute request counts and use rolling median smoothing
Risk: cross-traffic contamination in shared pipelines —> Mitigation: enforce header-based routing and sampling buckets
Risk: regression in hallucination/quality not captured by simple metrics —> Mitigation: require prompt set evaluations and human spot checks on each stage
Risk: dashboards not instrumented in time —> Mitigation: shipping conservative default thresholds and enabling mute/unmute controls
dashboards_and_alerts: Canonical experiment dashboard: latency, errors, cost, quality delta (by prompt group)
Canary alert: sustained deviation beyond SLA for 15m (pager to SRE on P0, slack for PM for P1)
Ramp alert: cumulative cost delta > 20% vs baseline over 24h triggers review
Quality regression alert: prompt set delta > threshold for two consecutive windows
